alternatives: The consistent sign across four whales could still arise from a shared recording or preprocessing pipeline rather than a biologically general pattern.
The mixed-model fit may be influenced by the MLE boundary warning, so the estimated coefficient could be biased or inflated.
hypothesis.claim: For every whale in the frozen cohort, the within-whale raw difference a_minus_i is positive (ATWOOD 0.148, FORK 0.159, PINCHY 0.072, TBB 0.168) and the normalized z_diff is positive, matching the pooled negative vowel_code coefficient (-0.1318, p ~ 3.7e-11); this supports a consistent, same-direction vowel-associated effect across whales rather than a single-whale driver.
falsifiers: Adding more whales produces at least one whale with a negative raw_diff_a_minus_i exceeding the positive ones in magnitude.
Re-fitting without the boundary condition yields a coefficient whose sign or significance no longer matches the per-whale direction.
The per-whale effects are shown to be an artifact of unequal n_a vs n_i sampling within whales.
limitations: n_groups = 4 is a very small number of random-effect levels for a mixed model.
The MLE boundary warning indicates the estimate may lie near the edge of the parameter space, limiting inferential strength.
The gate artifact is a reproduction check with frozen thresholds and does not by itself establish generalization beyond this cohort.
hypothesis.title: Within-whale monotone a>i effect across all four whales drives the pooled vowel contrast

alternatives: The rate difference could reflect a per-whale production-style effect rather than a vowel-associated phonological contrast, since only four whales contribute.
The click_rate_hz contrast could be an artifact of duration normalization (duration_z) rather than an independent rate parameter.
hypothesis.claim: In the frozen cohort, codas labeled with vowel 'a' are produced at a lower click_rate_hz than codas labeled 'i' (a_minus_i = -0.542 Hz, 95% CI entirely below zero), and this rate difference co-occurs with longer mean_ici_s for 'a' (a_minus_i = +0.0337 s, CI above zero), consistent with 'a'-labeled codas having more spaced click train timing rather than merely more clicks.
falsifiers: A re-partition with additional whales whose a_minus_i click_rate_hz CI includes zero.
Demonstration that the click_rate_hz contrast disappears after conditioning on mean_ici_s or click_count within this frozen cohort.
Evidence that the vowel labels are not comparable across whales (e.g., differing annotation conventions).
limitations: Only four whales are represented in whale_feature_means and partition_contrasts (n_whales = 4); no broad population inference is possible.
All sampled records come from ATWOOD and share coda_type '1+1+3', so the contrast is not shown to generalize across coda types.
spectral_quality, formants, and edge_coarticulation are 'not_observable' in this run, so articulatory interpretations are unavailable.
hypothesis.title: Vowel-conditioned click-rate contrast with lengthened a-intervals

alternatives: The npvi contrast, though CI-positive, could be dominated by a few high-NPVI outlier records rather than a systematic a/i distribution shift.
The terminal_ici_ratio contrast could reflect a boundary or segmentation artifact at the end of codas rather than a phonological property of the vowel partition.
hypothesis.claim: Within the frozen cohort, 'a'-labeled codas show higher timing variability than 'i'-labeled codas on two independent dispersion features: npvi (a_minus_i = +2.14, CI above zero) and ici_cv (a_minus_i = +0.031, CI above zero), while terminal_ici_ratio is lower for 'a' (a_minus_i = -0.0129, CI below zero), suggesting the vowel partition covaries with rhythmic dispersion and with the terminal inter-click interval specifically.
falsifiers: Recomputing the contrasts with outlier-trimmed records yields CIs spanning zero for npvi and/or ici_cv.
The terminal_ici_ratio effect reverses sign in an independent cohort with different segmentation parameters.
The npvi and ici_cv effects are found to be driven by click_count rather than vowel label.
limitations: npvi has a notably wider bootstrap CI (low 0.256, high 4.017) than ici_cv, so its magnitude is less precisely estimated.
The sample shown is deterministic but limited; per-record outliers (e.g., a record with npvi ~133.9) may influence aggregates.
Feature definitions and normalization were fixed by an upstream artifact (normalization hash), so alternate normalizations were not explored.
hypothesis.title: Rhythm-variability (NPVI and ICI-CV) increase in a-labeled codas
